To return the mate of v, inspect its at most Δ incident edges with the consistent edge-membership oracle. Thus a source cost Q gives O(Δ²(Q+1)) ordinary probes per mate query. These are probes, not distributed LOCAL rounds or CPU time. Theorem 17 states Q=(log* n)^{⌈1/ε⌉+1}·2^{Δ^{O(1/ε)}} for deterministic stateless edge membership. Unit weights turn the cardinality guarantee into the identical total-weight guarantee. This is a compatible baseline beside the unit-weight lower bound; it is not claimed to be the fastest cardinality LCA.

slices.label: Matching edges and bounded-weight estimation
slices.task: Compare explicit maximum-weight matching with additive estimation of optimal weight in separate panels.
assumptions: WeightedNeighbor(v,i) returns the i-th neighbor together with its edge weight, or ⊥ past the end of the fixed list. The n labeled vertices are known. No free edge list or global weight table. Arbitrary-weight matching and [0,1]-weight additive estimation are distinct output contracts.

results.sourceLocation: Edmonds, Theorems (P), (M), and §7; exact query accounting is an atlas composition.
results.notes: Read each vertex list until the first ⊥. There are 2m successful weighted-neighbor replies and n terminal replies, hence exactly n+2m queries. Deduplicate the two copies of each edge and solve the stored weighted graph. Query cost is not computation time.

slices.label: Matching edges and bounded-weight estimation
slices.task: Compare explicit maximum-weight matching with additive estimation of optimal weight in separate panels.
assumptions: WeightedPair(u,v) returns the edge weight, including zero, or a distinct absence symbol ⊥. The n labeled vertices are known. One query reveals one unordered pair; no degree or neighbor oracle. Arbitrary-weight matching and [0,1]-weight additive estimation are distinct output contracts.

results.sourceLocation: Edmonds, Theorems (P), (M), and §7; exact query accounting is an atlas composition.
results.notes: Read every unordered pair u<v exactly once. There are n(n−1)/2 such pairs. Retain all present weighted edges and solve the stored weighted graph. Query cost is not computation time.

results.guarantee: OPT ≤ estimate ≤ OPT+εn, with probability at least 2/3. This is additive error, not a fixed multiplicative ratio.
results.sourceLocation: Nguyen–Onak, Definition 3 and §1.5 Maximum Weight Matching, PDF page 3. Matrix access is an elementary oracle simulation.
results.notes: To answer a simulated indexed-neighbor request, scan that vertex’s matrix row and order its present neighbors by vertex label; cache the row. Each simulated request costs at most n−1 pair queries, so f(Δ,ε) requests cost at most (n−1)f(Δ,ε). The theorem’s probability and additive error are unchanged. Full enumeration is always an alternative. The displayed O(n) class fixes Δ and ε.
